evals.prompt: Create a new ASP.NET Core MVC app called Acme.Web and wire it to Kontent.ai environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. Generate strongly typed models for it, but don't invent any pages from the content model yet - I just want the plumbing in place.
evals.expected_output: A solution with an MVC project from the standard template on an installed stable SDK; stable, mutually compatible Kontent.Ai.Delivery, Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration and Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore packages; a local tool manifest pinning Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator; generated models in a dedicated directory; DeliveryOptions bound in Program.cs through the builder callback; tag helpers registered; a green build; and no controllers, views or routes derived from content types.
assertions: A .config/dotnet-tools.json manifest pins Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator
Generated model files carry the auto-generated header and a [ContentTypeCodename] attribute

The web project references Kontent.Ai.Delivery, Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration and Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore from one package line (the current release-candidate line unless the user or framework forces the previous stable one)

Program.cs registers the client with the AddDeliveryClient form that matches the resolved Delivery major (builder callback on 20.x, IConfiguration overload on 19.x) and binds the DeliveryOptions section
_ViewImports.cshtml contains @addTagHelper *, Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore
No controller, view or route was created for a content type
dotnet build completes with zero errors
No Preview or Secure Access API key appears in any file in the output

evals.prompt: Add Kontent.ai Delivery to the existing MVC solution in existing-net10-cpm (Acme.slnx) using environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. Keep our target framework and central package management exactly as they are.
evals.expected_output: Kontent.ai packages added as PackageVersion entries in Directory.Packages.props with version-less PackageReference items in Acme.Web.csproj; TargetFramework unchanged; models generated into the web project; DeliveryOptions bound in Program.cs; a green build; and no edits to files unrelated to the integration.
assertions: Acme.Web.csproj still targets net10.0
Directory.Packages.props contains PackageVersion entries for every Kontent.ai package added
No PackageReference in Acme.Web.csproj carries an inline Version attribute
Generated models exist in a dedicated directory inside the web project and compile
Program.cs registers the client with the AddDeliveryClient form that matches the resolved Delivery major and binds the DeliveryOptions section
dotnet build completes with zero errors
Files unrelated to the integration (HomeController.cs, existing views, wwwroot) are unchanged

evals.prompt: Scaffold a Kontent.ai MVC app for environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019 and then implement a listing page and a detail page for the Article content type. Keep the Delivery DTO handling out of the controllers, and render the article body rich text and the article image with the Kontent.ai ASP.NET Core helpers.
evals.expected_output: A working vertical slice: a content service that owns IDeliveryClient queries and maps to view models, a thin controller that returns NotFound for a missing item, Razor views using the rich-text and img-asset tag helpers, typed queries with the request cancellation token, a green build, and no global navigation or site structure invented beyond the article pages.
assertions: A service or similar class depends on IDeliveryClient and builds the Article queries; no controller references IDeliveryClient or IDeliveryResult
The detail query passes the request CancellationToken to ExecuteAsync
A missing article (StatusCode NotFound) results in the controller returning NotFound(), while other failed results are logged or thrown rather than rendered as empty content
The listing query uses GetItems<Article>() with element projection or ordering via the generated codename constants
The detail view renders the body with a rich-text tag helper rather than raw HTML output
The article image asset is rendered with an img-asset tag helper
No navigation menu, homepage composition or routes for content types other than Article were invented
dotnet build completes with zero errors

evals.prompt: Build the whole website represented by this Kontent.ai environment: 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that navigation, URL hierarchy and page composition cannot be derived from content-type names, inspects the environment enough to propose a bounded first slice (or asks which routable type to implement), and does not silently generate a site map, menu and routes for every content type.
assertions: The response states that a full site cannot be inferred from the content model alone
The agent either asks the user which content type to start with or recommends one specific bounded first slice
No navigation menu or URL hierarchy spanning multiple content types was generated without confirmation
Any code that was produced compiles

evals.prompt: Generate the MVC integration for our secured Kontent.ai environment <environment-id>. I've exported the Secure Access key as KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY in this shell - use it, but make sure it never ends up in the repo, in a command, or in your summary.
evals.expected_output: Requires a real Secure Access environment; replace <environment-id> and export KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY before running. The agent checks the variable is present without printing it, passes it to the model generator and to user-secrets by variable reference only, enables UseSecureAccess in tracked configuration, and neither prints nor commits the key.
assertions: The Secure Access key value does not appear in any file under the output directory
The Secure Access key value does not appear in the agent's final report or in any command it ran; commands reference $KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY by name
The model generator was invoked with --DeliveryOptions:UseSecureAccess true and the key passed by variable reference
The application stores SecureAccessApiKey in user secrets or reads it from an environment variable, and UseSecureAccess is true in the tracked DeliveryOptions section
dotnet build completes with zero errors

evals.prompt: Add the latest Kontent.ai MVC integration to the Legacy.Web app in existing-net8. It's on net8.0 and we can't move it right now.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps net8.0 and installs the newest stable net8.0-compatible releases (Delivery 19.x, AspNetCore 0.16.x) with a matching model generator, gets a green build, and explains the framework constraint and the upgrade path in the report.
assertions: Legacy.Web.csproj still targets net8.0
No Kontent.ai package reference uses a prerelease version
The installed Kontent.ai packages restore successfully on net8.0 (no NU1202)
The report explains which package line was chosen and why, and names a framework upgrade as a separate choice if a newer line requires it
dotnet build completes with zero errors

evals.prompt: Create a React frontend with an ASP.NET Core BFF that reads content from Kontent.ai environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises that this skill targets server-rendered MVC and does not apply the Razor recipe: no Razor views or tag helpers for content rendering, and a clear statement that the BFF/SPA architecture needs a different approach (it may still set up the Delivery client for an API project).
assertions: The response states that this MVC skill does not fit a React plus BFF architecture
No Razor views, _ViewImports tag-helper registration or rich-text/img-asset markup were created for content rendering
If any Delivery client registration was produced, it uses the AddDeliveryClient form that matches the resolved Delivery major

evals.prompt: The content model changed - regenerate the Kontent.ai models in the Acme.Web app in regenerate-net10 and make sure nothing stale is left behind.
evals.expected_output: Models regenerated with the pinned local tool into a temporary directory and diffed against Content/Generated; the stale LegacyBanner.cs record is removed; the hand-written partial Content/Article.cs is preserved; the project rebuilds; and the summary lists removed or renamed types.
assertions: Content/Generated/LegacyBanner.cs no longer exists after regeneration
Content/Article.cs (the hand-written partial) is unchanged
Every file remaining in Content/Generated carries the auto-generated header
The tool manifest's pinned Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator version was used, not a global install or a different version
The report lists the content types that were removed or renamed
dotnet build completes with zero errors
